label: Efficient causing in a history at a moment, and self-giving as efficient self-causation there
term: efficient causing in a history at a moment (Lean parameter `EfficientlyCausesAt`)
definition: EfficientlyCausesAt v t c x r: in history v at moment t, c is an efficient cause of x's being r. For each fixed v and t it is the here-and-now efficient causing of EFFICIENT_CAUSING_2 (definition 69c0b23e), read in that history at that moment; the indices make explicit what 69c0b23e leaves implicit (one world, one time). SelfGivingIsEfficientSelfCauseAt F EfficientlyCausesAt w: for every history v accessible from w, candidate c and moment t, if F.GivesAt v c c t (c exercises strict giving of its own esse at t in v, definition 158301bc) then EfficientlyCausesAt v t c c F.esse. Both indices are kept, so no causal exercise is moved between histories or moments. The bridge constrains only the self-edge and is weaker than an inclusion of GivesAt in efficient causing for all c and x. Distinct from F.CausesIn (cause of a perfection), from the tenseless EfficientlyCausesEsse (8934912c) and from a world- and time-neutral efficient relation.
note: Analyst stipulation, attribution deferred. Replaces the index-free bridge SelfGivingIsEfficientSelfCause, whose consequent dropped the history and moment of GivesAt and so required re-reading the selected-time Second Way premises modally (semantic re-check on #1863). EfficientlyCausesAt is a supplied primitive relation: no structural law (irreflexivity, asymmetry, transitivity) is assumed; no self-causation and cause priority enter as the separate OPEN premises NoEfficientSelfCauseOnAccessible and EfficientCauseIsPriorOnAccessible. Whether strict self-giving of being would be efficient self-causation is the OPEN content of the bridge. The indexed omission control (IndexedCertificate) keeps both Second Way premises while falsifying the bridge and no-self-giving.
